**Company Description**

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

 **Job Description**

AI Security Incubation & Innovation

Security and Risk Engineering

About the team

The Security and Risk Engineering organization builds scalable, AI-powered security solutions that reduce risk and protect ServiceNow and its customers. We value AI-first thinking, clean architecture, intuitive experiences, and a culture of continuous learning.

This is a zero-to-one incubation. We're building a new class of exposure analysis that ranks security work by exploitability (where an attacker could realistically get in) rather than raw severity. The architecture is evolving, and you'll help build it.

The role

As an ML Engineer, you'll build and ship LLM-powered features for a new exploitability engine. That means the services, retrieval pipelines and agent workflows that turn raw security signal into ranked, reachable attack paths. You'll work on well-scoped problems with senior engineers, learn how production AI systems are built and run, and take on more ownership as you grow.

What you'll own

* Well-scoped features and components, from design to production, with guidance from senior engineers.
* The quality of what you ship: tests, evals and monitoring that show your work does what it should.
* Pieces of the AI plumbing, such as prompts, retrieval, tool integrations and data connectors, and keeping them reliable.
* LLMs/Agentic AI and MLOps are relevant, let's include those

What you'll do

* Build backend services and APIs in Python that connect LLMs to enterprise security data.
* Build LLM features using prompt engineering, structured outputs, tool/function calling, and retrieval (RAG, embeddings, vector search).
* Help build and extend agent workflows that retrieve information, call tools, and recover from failures.
* Write evals and automated tests that measure accuracy, latency and cost.
* Build connectors that bring security evidence (vulnerability scanners, identity systems, asset inventories) into the platform.
* Use AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex or Devin every day, and review their output carefully.
* Prototype quickly to test new AI capabilities against real security problems.
* Take part in code and design reviews, and learn the security domain from security R&D and SecOps partners.
* What you bring
* Strong Python. This is a must.
* Solid software engineering fundamentals: data structures, APIs, testing, debugging.
* Hands-on experience building something with LLMs, at work or in a substantial project: RAG, embeddings, tool calling or agents.
* Experience calling at least one frontier model API or SDK (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or equivalent).
* Curiosity about security and a willingness to learn the domain on the job.
* Clear communication, and comfort asking questions in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.
* You don't need a background in classical ML, statistics or data science.
* Nice to have
* Experience with AWS, Azure or GCP, containers, or CI/CD.
* Exposure to AI evaluation, observability or guardrails.
* Experience with vector databases or search.
* Any exposure to security: vulnerability management, identity, threat detection, CTFs or coursework.
* Open-source contributions.

  
**Qualifications**

Qualifications

* 2+ years of software engineering experience, or equivalent practical experience.
* Strong programming experience in Python.
* Experience building or integrating LLM-powered applications, in production or in substantial projects.
* Working knowledge of APIs, databases and cloud-native development.
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

What success looks like

* Ship: Take a scoped feature from ticket to production with tests and evals in place.
* Build AI-native: Choose the right LLM technique for a problem, and know when not to use one.
* Learn fast: Get productive in the codebase and the security domain quickly.
* Grow: Need less guidance over time and take on bigger parts of the system.

---------------

Amazon’s Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) is building the next generation of quantum computing hardware.
  
  
The Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) is our longest-horizon bet and operates at the intersection of hardware and physics. The goal is a quantum computer that could solve in hours what today's most robust machines would take thousands of years to compute, unlocking breakthroughs in myriad of areas ranging from advanced materials for batteries to cryptography and fundamentally-secure data sharing protocols. This program involves R&D in device theory, materials science, nano-scale fabrication, superconducting circuit design, cryogenic refrigeration, and quantum algorithms and applications.

**About Ande**

We're a Series A startup building an AI-native platform that connects Enterprises and Hospitality across the entire booking experience, backed by top-tier investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, Sierra Ventures, and Bain Capital, and led by a serial entrepreneur with offices in NYC and SF. We help companies turn every dinner, event, and offsite into something effortless to plan and a breeze to manage, plugging right into the tools they already use.

**About the Role**

You will own the intelligence behind the Ande Agent. That's the concierge and its team of subagents that take a request from one sentence ("dinner for 12 with the Acme team next Thursday, somewhere private") to a confirmed, paid, on-policy booking. Along the way they source venues, compare options, email the venue and negotiate terms, and handle every change after that.

This is not a chatbot or a demo. The agent acts on real money, on behalf of real executives, with real venues on the other end of the thread. It runs in production today for reservations and private dining. Our strategy depends on carrying more of the work with every request: more kinds of entertainment, more cities, more of the workflow, without growing headcount to match. You will set how we get there.

**What You'll Do**

* Own the agent system. Ande runs on a root concierge agent with specialist subagents for sourcing, comparison, and venue coordination, on a self-hosted agent harness behind queued turn workers. You’ll own its architecture, model choices, and upgrade path, and make sure it holds up under latency budgets, provider failover, and real-world load.
* Build tools the agent can trust. The agent has about 75 typed capabilities that let it search, hold, book, pay, and message. Each one runs as the acting user and respects who they’re acting for, such as an assistant booking on behalf of an executive. Consequential actions become proposals that the booker confirms. You’ll decide what the agent is allowed to do, and how to make it safe.
* Make evals the gate for every change. You’ll build scenario suites, graders, and LLM judges calibrated against human labels. They replay from recorded runs on every PR and run in full nightly. Your goal is evals trustworthy enough that a model upgrade or prompt change can ship on the strength of the number alone, and cheap enough to run all the time.
* Power venue correspondence. Our agent negotiates with venues over email. It reads replies, pulls out offers, minimums, deadlines, and payment requests, and knows when to push, when to wait, and when to hand off to a person. You’ll make sure all of it is resistant to anything a third party writes into a thread.
* Build memory and the supply learning loop. You’ll shape what the agent remembers about a company, its people, and its venues, with clear rules on what’s shared and what stays private. You’ll also build the loop that turns every venue conversation into structured supply data, like which room actually fits 14 or what a venue will do on a Tuesday, so each recommendation is better than the last.
* Ship fast, reliable judgments. You’ll build typed classifiers for consent, triage, ranking, and urgency. Each has labeled thresholds, a timeout, and a fallback, and each rolls out from shadow mode to live.
* Set the bar for building with AI. You’ll define how Ande builds with AI: agent behavior as versioned config, product teammates proposing changes through evals, and AI coding agents as the default way the team ships. You’ll mentor engineers and partner closely with our AI product manager.

**What We’re Looking For**

* Education and experience: a degree in Computer Science or Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. You have 5+ years building production software, including 2+ years shipping LLM agents to real customers (tool use, multi-step planning, structured outputs, long-running conversations).
* Production evals: you’ve owned evals in production, from writing them to finding failure modes in real traffic and improving quality turn by turn.
* Systems engineering: strong TypeScript and backend skills, including queues, concurrency, idempotency, and how distributed systems fail.
* Sound judgment: you know where a model belongs and where deterministic code does, and you have the discipline to make agent actions safe, auditable, and reversible.
* AI-native workflow: you use AI coding agents every day. Our codebase is built to be worked on by them, and we expect you to raise that bar.
* Clear communication: you can explain agent behavior and trade-offs to product, operations, and customers.

**Bonus Points**

* You've been a founding or early engineer and know how to balance craft, ownership and speed.
* You've built agent harnesses, orchestration layers or tool brokers, not just prompts.
* Experience with search, ranking or recommendation systems.
* Experience with marketplaces, booking or payments, where a wrong action costs money.
* Experience defending agents against prompt injection from untrusted content.

**Why This Role Matters**

The Ande Agent is how we scale. Every request it handles end to end is work we don’t have to hire for, so how far it can take us depends on the person who owns its intelligence.

The stakes are real. The agent moves real money for executives and negotiates directly with venues, so a mistake costs customers money and costs us venue relationships. Every venue conversation also makes the agent smarter. That learning loop is an advantage competitors can’t easily copy.

This isn’t an AI feature bolted onto a product. The agent is the product, and you’ll own how it thinks.

* Experience with AWS, Azure or GCP, containers, or CI/CD.

Qualifications

We're looking for engineers who love reasoning about permission models as much as building intuitive interfaces. You'll work at the intersection of product, design, and engineering to turn a relationship-based authorization system into tools that let admins control access with confidence and let users understand exactly why they can or can't see something. Success in this role is measured by building products that make a precise, deny-by-default permission model legible without hiding its power.

  
  

You'll partner closely with backend engineers, designers, and product teams to define workflows, shape product direction, and make thoughtful technical tradeoffs in an environment where requirements are often ambiguous and the best solutions aren't immediately obvious. You'll own the auth frontend largely end to end, so your judgment will shape how access control feels across the whole product.

**Make permissions visible across the product**

Bring the permission model into every part of the app so that what users see matches what they're allowed to do, from hiding actions they can't take to explaining why. You'll also build the sign-in experiences that connect Nominal to customers' enterprise identity providers.

  
  

**Own ambiguous product problems**
